title: Baison E3 - ExecByControlName_Two Unauthenticated Arbitrary SQL Execution (leading to RCE)
vendor_detail: 上海百胜软件股份有限公司
product: E3 全渠道中台 (E3 Omni-channel Retail Platform)
version_detail: confirmed on buildTime 20260929 (productCode 1008) and a productCode 1011 deployment; reported affected range V2.3.0-T5 .. V2.5.1-T6 (boundaries not independently verified)

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

cvss.scenario: Unauthenticated remote attacker; single HTTP request with an offline-computable signature

impact_note: SQL execution confirmed with echo; on deployments running the database connection as sa with xp_cmdshell enabled (verified on one live deployment: value_in_use = 1), the same endpoint accepts EXEC batches, yielding remote code execution by configuration-state confirmation. Command execution was not exercised on third-party systems.

affected.note: range reported during assessment; boundaries not independently verified

description: A vulnerability classified as critical has been found in Baison E3 全渠道中台. Affected by this issue is the ExecByControlName_Two endpoint of the KHATTACH controller. The endpoint reflectively invokes a backend method named by the client-supplied controleName and method fields without authentication and passes retObjs[0], an arbitrary attacker-controlled string, directly to the backend SQL Server as a T-SQL batch; EXEC statements are accepted. The request signature md5(timestamp + AccessToken + UserID + wcfService + dataJson + SIGN_KEY) relies on a key (5feb28f6a28613ace02fe261c6b6c294) hard-coded in the public frontend JavaScript bundle and shared across deployments, with AccessToken and UserID accepted empty, so signatures can be forged offline. Requests without an En-Status header bypass the AES request-body gateway entirely. The database connection runs as sa (sysadmin confirmed); on one verified deployment xp_cmdshell is enabled (value_in_use = 1), making unauthenticated remote code execution reachable. The same product also exposes an unauthenticated SQL-injection endpoint (POST /e3api/api/main/getCacheDataFromDB, string-concatenated selectFields/tableName/where) and an unauthenticated full system-parameter disclosure endpoint (POST /e3api/api/SysInfo/SysParamInfo, including IAM_SECRET and PLAT_* platform credentials).

vulnerable_code.snippet:
controleName = "mod_ComFunc"
method       = "GetDataBySql_Two"   (also "GetDataBySql")
retObjs[0]   = <arbitrary T-SQL batch, executed by SQL Server and echoed back>
requests carrying an En-Status header are decrypted; requests without the header are passed through as plaintext multipart with no access control

attack_vector: The attacker sends a single multipart POST to /e3api/api/KHATTACH/ExecByControlName_Two with empty AccessToken/UserID/wcfService fields, a self-chosen millisecond timestamp, a data JSON of {"controleName":"mod_ComFunc","method":"GetDataBySql_Two","retObjs":["<SQL>"]}, and Sign computed offline with the publicly extractable hard-coded key. The En-Status header is simply omitted. retObjs[0] is executed by the backend SQL Server and the result is echoed in the HTTP response. No credentials of any kind are used.

stage_1.effect: returns {"A":[{"e3probe":{"Int32":1},...}]} - anonymous SQL execution with echo

reproduction_environment.stack: Baison E3 全渠道中台 deployments (frontend + e3api + SQL Server 2019 on Windows Server 2019)
reproduction_environment.targets: one vendor demo deployment and two independent live deployments (hostnames withheld); productCode 1008 / 1011
reproduction_environment.note: verification limited to read-only statements; command execution confirmed by configuration state only

timeline.event: Vulnerability identified during an authorized assessment of a demo deployment and reproduced on two independent live deployments
